request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the policy versions: one line per version, oldest first, as <version> <from or start>
<key>=<value> <count of claims whose policy version it is>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The screen now has a policy versions list, and all 4 Playwright tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

Pressing **Show policy versions** (`policy-show`) lists one `policy-line` per version, oldest first, as `<version> <from or start> <key>=<value> <count>`, for example `3 2026-02-01 rounding=half-up 1`.

- **Stored data:** policy versions didn't record the value they set, so I added a value column. The new migration `V125__policy_version_value.sql` fills it in for existing versions from the dated setting with the same key and from-date. If that setting was later changed on the same date, the old version picks up the newer value. New versions store their value when saved, and cloning a sheet copies it.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{id}/settings/policy`, returns each version with its claim count. A claim counts towards the version in force on its date, which is the same rule the existing per-claim policy column uses. Voided claims are included, as the third scenario expects.
- **Front end:** a new small component, `features/policy/policy-versions.ts`, placed on the home screen. It asks the server each time the button is pressed, so the counts are current. If the request fails it shows a `policy-error` message.

A version with no from-date shows `start`, and a setting with no value (such as no clerk limit) shows as `key=` with nothing after it. Nothing is written to the audit file.
